newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada and Chile sign free trade agreement.
newsitem.headline: Canada and Chile sign free trade agreement.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien and Chilean President Eduardo Frei on Monday signed a free trade agreement between their two countries.
The accord, which followed 11 months of negotiations, is seen as a stepping stone for Chile to become a member of the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA).
"This agreement demonstrates Canada's determination to create jobs and encourage economic growth through trade liberalisation," Chretien said at the signing ceremony.
NAFTA groups Canada, the United States and Mexico, and some of the provisions of the agreement between Ottawa and Santiago were modelled on similar NAFTA clauses.
Chile is Canada's fourth largest export partner in South America. Canadian exports to Chile totalled C$387 million (US$286 million) in 1995.

Some C$666 million (US$483 million) worth of goods were traded between the two countries in 1995 and under the new agreement this could double, Canadian International Trade Minister Art Eggleton said last week.
The pact calls for the removal of tariffs on 75 percent of trade between Chile and Canada as soon as it goes into effect, with most other tariffs to be phased out over five years.
